# Chegg, Inc.

### Case Details

**Class Period:** May 5, 2020 - November 1, 2021

**Date Filed:** December 22, 2021

**Case Number:** 5:21-cv-9953

**Jurisdiction:** Northern District of California

**Case Type:** Securities Case

### Case Summary

Saxena White was appointed Co-Lead Counsel in the securities fraud class action against Chegg and certain of its senior executives for violations of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The Complaint alleges that Chegg made materially false and misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about the Company’s business, operations, and prospects, thus artificially inflating the Company’s stock price and causing investors to suffer substantial losses when the truth eventually emerged.

Chegg is an online learning platform that provides educational resources such as online tutoring, study materials, and textbook rentals. Chegg purports to “help students master their subjects, better understand their course material, and have better outcomes on their learning journey.” In particular, Chegg features an “Expert Q&A” service that allows subscribers to ask a pool of approximately 100,000 experts for an “instantaneous step-by-step solution” to “homework” questions.

# Chegg Inc. stock down 99% since ChatGPT. Is it a GenAI casualty or hype fallout?

This title was summarized by AI from the post below.

[Phil Laufenberg](https://au.linkedin.com/in/philipplaufenberg?trk=public_post_feed-actor-name)

* [Report this post](/uas/login?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fposts%2Fphilipplaufenberg_chegg-inc-is-a-live-case-study-worth-watching-activity-7327840680737730561-BN3B&trk=public_post_ellipsis-menu-semaphore-sign-in-redirect&guestReportContentType=POST&_f=guest-reporting)

[Chegg Inc.](https://www.linkedin.com/company/chegg-inc-?trk=public_post-text) is a live case study worth watching. Its stock is down 99% since ChatGPT launched. GenAI casualty or just hype fallout? Every time there’s a major GenAI release, someone screams: “XYZ is dead.” Chegg has been on that list. They built a business on tutoring and millions of curated Q&A pairs. Most of which can now allegedly be answered by free tools like ChatGPT. So why would anyone still pay for Chegg? Turns out, a lot of people don’t. They’ve lost millions of users. The decline is very real and Wall Street has them priced for bankruptcy. And yet, 2 million people still pay! They turnover more than $100M per quarter. Institutional interest is growing. They’ve got cash runway left. And they are priced like a serious A startup with a dream. I’m seeing first-hand: ChatGPT isn’t always a great tutor. It looks right even when it’s confidently wrong. No scaffolding. No guided learning. Students often don’t know what they don’t know, and relying on ChatGPT can be dangerous. That might be where Chegg still has an edge. Once the hype settles, and if LLMs don’t materially improve, Chegg’s churned customers might come back. They just released Q1 numbers. If you’re in the education space, take a closer look and practice your critical thinking muscle. Maybe this is a massive overreaction. Maybe not. But it’s a fascinating real-time story about how education, AI, and business collide.…
